title: How would you estimate how many office chairs UK employers buy each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many office chairs do UK employers buy each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Business-to-business sizing: start from the number of desk workers and how long a chair lasts. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many office chairs do UK employers buy each year?

The approach

Desk workers ÷ years a chair lasts.

Tip: Say your approach out loud before any numbers; it lets the interviewer agree or nudge you early.

Step by step

  1. People working at a desk in the UK: 15M
  2. ÷ 7 years an office chair lasts

That gives about 2.14M chairs a year.

Does it make sense?

New offices and hybrid work move this up or down; replacement alone gives the base.

Count corporate purchases separately from home purchases

The estimate of 2.14 million annual chairs captures replacements for existing UK desk workers. It assumes one employer-provided chair per person and a seven-year life. It might miss spare chairs in meeting rooms or additional desks in new offices, while hybrid working may reduce the number of dedicated seats.

Try a sensitivity test: if employers replace chairs every ten years rather than seven, annual replacement demand falls from 2.14 million to 1.5 million. That is a difference of more than 600,000 units. Conversely, a large office-refurbishment cycle can create a temporary spike unrelated to normal replacement.

Clarify whether you include chairs bought by people for home offices, schools and government workplaces. If the client manufactures office furniture, a separate question is whether it sells through distributors or directly to employers, since revenue per chair differs across channels.
